label: one or two steps after an f in the early original phase
explanation: Fires during the original (input) phase at steps 1-4 when the letter f was input one step back (strongest; prev_tok=f alone covers ~79% of activation mass) or two steps back (weaker, decaying trace). Largest activations (near max) come at the step right after a second consecutive f (e.g. g f f [x]). The current input token barely matters. Rate falls off sharply after t=4 and is zero from t=6 on. Never fires in the copy phase and only rarely, weakly, at the delimiter. Missed activations are tiny (about 2% of mass); false positives are mostly two-steps-after-f positions at later t.

issues: The false positives follow a clean token rule, not noise. The two-steps-back branch (prev2_tok==f, prev_tok!=f, t<=4) has precision of only about 0.77. Split by the intervening token prev_tok, precision is about 0.94-0.99 for nearly every token, but it collapses for k (0.008), w (0.006), 2 (0.024), m (0.030), t (0.048) and y (0.18), and is partial for v (0.42). Each of these tokens has about 1.5k predicted steps on dev. So when one of these tokens follows the f, the trace from that f is cut off. This accounts for almost all of the roughly 11k test false positives (rendered examples include g q f [k] *b*, g d f [t] *j*, c f [m] *w*, m n f [w] *w*). The explanation dismisses these as 'positions two steps after an f where the feature stays off'. It never names the blocking-token class.

Claims that check out: prev_tok=f alone (t<=4) gives precision 0.99 and 78.5% of activation mass (the claimed ~79% is correct). There are zero copy-phase activations. At the delimiter, the rate is 0.3% and the mass share is 0.7%. The rate at t=5 is 1%, at t=6 there are 94 activations, and from t=7 on there are none. Note the claim 'zero from t=6 on' is slightly off: 94 activations occur at t=6. f f [x] with t<=4 has precision 1.0, which matches the top examples. Missed activations are about 3.3% of mass on test, small and scattered.
Reported test scores reproduce: P 0.897, R 0.818, F1 0.856, mass recall 0.967.
Adding the blocking-token exception raises test precision from 0.897 to 0.987, with no loss of mass recall.
skeptic.revised_label: one step after an f in the early original phase (t<=4); a weaker trace two steps after, unless the intervening token is k/m/t/w/y/2/v
